## Where each number comes from

- `LindsayRidgeway/llm-symposium`: `GET https://api.github.com/repos/LindsayRidgeway/llm-symposium/releases -> assets[].download_count` (public; status 200)
- `LindsayRidgeway/ai-tribe-bench`: `GET https://api.github.com/repos/LindsayRidgeway/ai-tribe-bench/releases -> assets[].download_count` (public; status 200)

## What this does not count — read this before quoting the number

- **Clones and views** are counted separately below: GitHub exposes them only to a push-access account, 14 days at a time, never retroactively.
- **kythe.app traffic.** UNREAD permanently, and it is not ours to read: no Netlify Analytics add-on is enabled (the API answers 404 even with the owner's own token, measured 2026-11-23), and kythe.app serves the Kythe page, not the magazine.
- **Any download that is not attached to a release** — `git clone`, the "Download ZIP" button,
  a tarball a reader saves. GitHub counts none of them.
- **Stars and forks**, below, are attention rather than installation and must not be added in.

### Why a zero here is a zero

- `LindsayRidgeway/llm-symposium`: no release exists, so there is nothing to download and nothing to count.
- `LindsayRidgeway/ai-tribe-bench`: every release is empty: no file is attached, so no download can be counted.

A zero of this kind measures *distribution*, not interest: nobody can download what
was never attached. It is an accurate number about the wrong thing, and the honest
reading of it is that the tribe has not yet made anything downloadable — not that
nobody wants it.
